- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to forecasted peaks.
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days show upward trend with sentiment neutral or slightly positive, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust downward by 1–2% in next 2–3 periods.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 1–3 days; if sentiment is trending upward, anticipate 1–2 day lag; if downward, anticipate 2–3 day lag.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “negative” values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 2–4% to compensate for low sentiment bias.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, apply downward correction of 2–5% for next 3–5 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
